chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever makes a mistake in the Adhan by bringing forward or delaying (a phrase), he should return to the first one which he delayed until he completes it at its end.

key_terms.سَهَا: Erred / Made a mistake (by omission or delay)

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for correcting a mistake in the Adhan call to prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling, transmitted through the chain of prominent Kufan narrators like Zurarah and Hammad, underscores the precision required in the Adhan, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maintaining the integrity of ritual declarations. It establishes that minor errors do not invalidate the entire call but require a specific corrective procedure: returning to the missed phrase to ensure the sequence is complete and uninterrupted. This principle highlights the scholarly view that the Adhan is a structured act of worship where accuracy in recitation order is paramount.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who errs in the Azān, so he brings forward or delays (a sentence), he should return to the former which he had delayed until he completes upon its ending’.
en.sarwar: 15. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one by mistake, mixes up Adhan he repeats to correct the mix up all the way to the end.’”
